newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico sets up Sonora gas distribution region.
newsitem.headline: Mexico sets up Sonora gas distribution region.

text.p: The Mexican Energy Ministry on Wednesday announced plans to boost natural gas consumption in three cities in the northern Mexican state of Sonora.
It also said it would soon start accepting bids from companies interested in gas distribution rights there.

The state capital of Hermosillo and the cities of Guaymas and Empalme were designated as a single region for the purposes of the government's program to set up natural gas distribution zones and to reduce dependence on fuel oil and diesel.
More than 600,000 people live in the three cities.
The government is awarding concessions to private companies to distribute natural gas by geographic area, as part of its liberalization of gas transport, distribution and storage.

One concession has already been awarded for the Mexicali area, and bidding is under way on a second concession in the Chihuahua region. The Sonora region is the third to be established by the government.

"The supply of natural gas favors the industrial consolidation of Hermosillo and will aid regional development, by encouraging different companies with high energy consumption to locate in the region," the ministry said in a statement.
Hermosillo already houses many of the nation's auto parts, plastics and chemicals factories.
The state, located on the U.S.-Mexico border, consumes more than 25 billion kilocalories of energy a day, the ministry estimates.
Mexico's shift toward natural gas is part of a broader move to clean up pollution in larger cities.
The Energy Regulation Commission will open the bidding for gas distribution in the Sonora region "in the coming weeks", the ministry said.
The winning company or group of companies will receive a contract for 12 years of exclusive gas distribution.
